evidence.note: Wrote a boto3 test suite explicitly targeting edge cases: multipart ETag matching, ranged reads, custom metadata, object tagging, notification webhooks, anonymous bucket policies, and lifecycle rules — well beyond ad hoc pokes.
Installed boto3 and launched the actual server, then exercised it, reproducing real client conditions rather than assuming code works.
Ran the suite, added the requests library to also hit admin JSON APIs directly, and re-ran — exercising both data-plane and admin surfaces.
No concurrency/30-client stress test and no console DOM/testid verification anywhere; console (half the grade) is written but never verified against its testid contract.

reasoning: The agent goes clearly beyond anchor 5: it uses real boto3 to exercise the main data plane plus several targeted edge cases (multipart ETag, ranged reads, tagging, notifications, policies, lifecycle) and hits the admin API directly. But it falls short of anchor 8 because two of that anchor's three pillars are entirely absent — there is no concurrency test for the 30-client requirement and no console DOM/testid verification (nor presigned/UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD or audit-atomicity checks). Strong data-plane edge-case verification with major untested subsystems places this at a 6.
